newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton firms, talk emerges of extra exports.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton firms, talk emerges of extra exports.

text.p: Speculation the Indian government may allow extra exports of cotton helped Punjab varieties firm on the local market, dealers said.
There was a shortage of ready stocks of Punjab cotton which has kept the price firm recently, they said.

In the spot deals Punjab saw-ginned rose by 10 rupees at 1,850/1,900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 moved up by 20/25 rupees at 2,100/2,125 rupees per maund and Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees at 1,040/1,100 rupees per maund.
"Some of the state-owned agencies are nursing higher unsold stock and they are demanding more export while millers are opposing such demand," one broker said.
Meanwhile Gujarat varieties were quiet in a limited activity. Gujarat Kalyan was steady at 14,200/14,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) so was wagad cotton at 12,900/13,000 rupees per candy.
